title: Loaded resources are cached and shared by every user
description: load()/preload() and scene-embedded resources resolve to one cached instance per path, so mutating a material, curve, shape or custom Resource reached through one node changes every node and every scene instance using it, until it is explicitly duplicated or made unique.
example: var m := preload("res://red.tres"); m.albedo_color = Color.BLUE  # every user of red.tres turns blue
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#9603 (open, 80 reactions, 25 comments; reduz: "It is not clear when internal subresources are duplicated or remain shared") | #28246 (open, 0 reactions, 15 comments; editing a tool-script export modifies collision shapes of all instances)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/resources.html "When the engine loads a resource from disk, it only loads it once. If a copy of that resource is already in memory, trying to load the resource again will return the same copy every time." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_resourceloader.html CACHE_MODE_REUSE: "The main resource (the one requested to be loaded), its subresources, and its dependencies (external resources) are retrieved from cache if present, instead of loaded."
evidence_source: core/io/resource_loader.cpp:800-810 (CACHE_MODE_REUSE returns the existing ResourceCache entry) | doc/classes/ResourceLoader.xml:86 (future load() calls use the cached version)
frequency: One web search ("godot changing material on one instance changes all instances forum") returned 7 distinct forum threads asking this in the top 9 (e.g. forum.godotengine.org/t/how-to-change-materials-in-a-single-instance/32584, godotforums.org/d/36712, /d/34276, /d/20521, /d/34044); proposal #9603 80 reactions
fix_reason: The cache is engine behavior every language inherits, but a language can type resources obtained via load/preload/exports as shared (read-only or copy-before-write) and provide an explicit make-unique operation on public Resource.duplicate*/ResourceLoader cache modes.

title: Resource.duplicate() depth: shallow by default, "deep" skips external and (before 4.5) collection-held subresources
description: duplicate() shares nested Array/Dictionary/Resource values; duplicate(true) copies only built-in (path-less) subresources, never external .tres ones, and before 4.5 did not copy Resources inside Array/Dictionary properties at all; 4.5 adds duplicate_deep() with a separate NONE/INTERNAL/ALL mode set.
example: var c := card.duplicate(true); c.effects[0].power = 9  # pre-4.5, or if effects[0] is an external .tres: the original card changes too
evidence_issues: #74918 (closed 2025-05-27 by PR #100673 "Overhaul resource duplication", milestone 4.5; 120 reactions, 40 comments) | #105904, #96627, #102902 (closed referencing #74918 as duplicate) | #82348 (closed, 5 comments) | #111130 (open, 8 comments; AnimationLibrary Make Unique not deep) | #123646 (open, 4 comments; @tool resources share Array/PackedArray after Make Unique) | godot-proposals#14859 (open, 8 comments, "Improve Resource.duplicate() method")
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-method-duplicate "If deep is false, a shallow copy is returned: nested Array, Dictionary, and Resource properties are not duplicated and are shared with the original resource." | same page: "Any Resource found inside will only be duplicated if it's local, like DEEP_DUPLICATE_INTERNAL used with duplicate_deep."
evidence_source: core/io/resource.cpp:296-305 (subresource copied by mode: NONE never, INTERNAL only if deep && is_built_in(), ALL if deep) | core/io/resource.cpp:517-529 (duplicate(deep) always uses RESOURCE_DEEP_DUPLICATE_INTERNAL) | core/io/resource.cpp:310-314 (Script subresources never duplicated)
frequency: #74918 120 reactions plus 3 issues closed as its duplicates (search "duplicate of #74918"); proposal #9603 80 reactions on the same confusion
status: partly fixed (PR #100673, 4.5: collection-held subresources, duplicate_deep); external subresources stay shared under duplicate(true) by design
fix_reason: Copy depth can be made explicit in the language's API (shallow / internal / all) and implemented on public Resource.duplicate_deep plus get_property_list/get/set, without engine changes.

title: Only @export/storage properties are saved and duplicated; plain vars silently reset
description: ResourceSaver, PackedScene packing, Resource.duplicate() and Node.duplicate() (by default) copy only properties with PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE; a GDScript var without @export/@export_storage carries no storage flag, so its value is lost on save/load and comes back as its initializer in duplicates.
example: class_name Inv extends Resource / var items := []  # never written to .tres, not copied by duplicate()
evidence_issues: #3393 (closed 2025-11-13 by PR #57121 "Add DUPLICATE_INTERNAL_STATE flag", milestone 4.6; 34 reactions, 26 comments) | #37222 (closed as duplicate of #3393, 12 comments) | #41417 (closed, "Resource.duplicate only duplicates exported variables") | #82857 (open, 7 comments; resource variables reset when duplicated before save)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_exports.html (@export_storage) "Also the property value is copied when Resource.duplicate() or Node.duplicate() is called, unlike non-exported variables." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html#class-node-method-duplicate "By default, this method will duplicate only properties marked for serialization (i.e. using PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE, or in GDScript, @export)."
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp:5420 (member PropertyInfo starts as PROPERTY_USAGE_NONE) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:2874-2908 (only exported vars take export usage; SCRIPT_VARIABLE added) | core/io/resource.cpp:408-411 (Resource::_duplicate skips non-STORAGE properties) | scene/main/node.cpp:3114 (Node duplicate skips non-STORAGE unless DUPLICATE_INTERNAL_STATE)
frequency: #3393 34 reactions; 3 further issues on the same behavior (#37222, #41417, #82857)
status: documented; Node: opt-in flag DUPLICATE_INTERNAL_STATE (PR #57121, 4.6); Resource.duplicate has no equivalent (by-design)
fix_reason: Which fields are persistent or copied is decided by the language's property list and its own instance data, so it can make persistence an explicit checked field modifier and copy full instance state via the script-instance get_property_state callback.

title: resource_local_to_scene only acts inside PackedScene.instantiate() and has gaps
description: Per-instance duplication happens only when a scene is instantiated (not for Resource.new(), runtime assignment, or flipping the flag later); before 4.5 it ignored resources inside Array/Dictionary (e.g. surface materials); Animation resources cannot be local to scene; in the editor it makes inherited scenes save duplicated copies as overrides.
example: node.stats = load("res://stats.tres")  # stats.tres is local_to_scene, but runtime assignment still shares it
evidence_issues: #71243 (closed 2024-02-29, 10 reactions; local to scene ignored for arrays/dicts incl. surface materials) | #90597 (closed 2025-07-03 by PR #108216, milestone 4.5; 6 reactions) | #82421 (open, 11 reactions, 18 comments, "Animations can no longer be local to scene"; #107970 closed as duplicate) | #94919 (open, 9 reactions; implicit overrides in inheriting scenes) | #111807 (open, 6 reactions, 14 comments) | #45350 (closed 2025-12-02; Node.duplicate copied the reference) | #55075 (closed not_planned)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_resource.html#class-resource-property-resource-local-to-scene "If true, the resource is duplicated for each instance of all scenes using it. At run-time, the resource can be modified in one scene without affecting other instances (see PackedScene.instantiate)." | "Note: Changing this property at run-time has no effect on already created duplicate resources."
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:509-514 (only values being set during instantiate pass through make_local_resource) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:537 and :554 (setup_resources_in_array/dictionary for collections, PR #108216) | core/io/resource.cpp:293-294 (local-scene duplication recurses only into sub-resources flagged local)
frequency: 64 issues with "local to scene" in the title (title search); top open ones 9-11 reactions
status: partly fixed (collections: PR #108216, 4.5); open: #82421, #94919, #111807; runtime-created resources by-design
fix_reason: A language can give fields per-instance resource semantics (duplicate on init/assignment via public duplicate_deep) regardless of the flag; instantiate-time handling, Animation support and editor overrides are engine/editor code.

title: Exported Array/Dictionary values from a scene were shared between instances (fixed only shallowly)
description: Collections saved in a .tscn belong to the SceneState; in 3.x, and for typed collections in 4.0-4.4, every instance got the same reference, so appending in one instance changed all of them and survived scene changes when the PackedScene was preloaded; since 4.5 each instance gets a shallow copy, so nested arrays/dictionaries inside stay shared; an unserialized exported typed-array default on a loaded .tres comes back read-only.
example: @export var tags: Array[String]  # filled in inspector / func _ready(): tags.append(name)  # 4.0-4.4: every instance sees all names
evidence_issues: #16478 (open, 12 reactions, 22 comments, "Exported (non-static) Arrays are not duplicated when instancing"; 2023 comment shows the typed-array regression in 4.x) | #103314 (closed 2025-07-03 by PR #108216 "Fix typed collections using same reference across scene instances", 4.5) | #94224 (open) | #17507, #52451, #45721, #44311, #36520, #65589 (closed referencing #16478 as duplicate) | #114342 (open, 4 reactions; exported Array default read-only when not serialized, 4.5-4.7)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_exports.html has no statement on sharing (page checked); a #16478 commenter (2024-01-14) notes "there is no mention of it"
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:523-537 (SceneState array shallow-duplicated or converted per instance since PR #108216) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:518-520 (inherited scenes use duplicate(true)) | nested containers staying shared: inferred from the shallow duplicate() at :531, unverified (needs repro)
frequency: #16478 plus 7 issues referencing it as duplicate (search "duplicate of #16478": 8 hits incl. itself)
fix_reason: The language's script-instance set callback receives the SceneState value and can copy it with the language's own collection semantics (value or deep copy), independent of what the engine passes.

title: Mutating a packed-array property in place silently edits a temporary copy
description: Engine getters return packed arrays by value, so line.points.append(p), points.clear(), points.resize(n) and points[0] = v change a temporary and are lost; GDScript writes back value-type chains such as position.x = 1 but skips write-back for packed arrays (counted as shared types) and never writes back after a method call, while the docs also say packed arrays are always passed by reference.
evidence_issues: #62857 (closed 2023-02-02, 6 comments) | #117962 (closed 2026-04-21 by PR #118002 adding a warning, milestone 4.7) | #117413 (closed 2026-03-14, 13 comments) | #104405 (open, 5 comments; resize has no effect; maintainer: "This is a known limitation and is documented") | #47060 (closed) | #70666 (closed not_planned) | #82577 (open, C#)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_packedvector2array.html "Note: Packed arrays are always passed by reference. ... This is not the case for built-in properties and methods. In these cases the returned packed array is a copy, and changing it will not affect the original value. To update a built-in property of this type, modify the returned array and then assign it to the property again."
evidence_source: scene/2d/line_2d.cpp:125 (get_points returns Vector<Vector2> by value) | core/variant/variant.cpp:3474-3491 (packed arrays reported as shared types) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:1177-1194 (assignment chain writes back only if type unknown or not shared) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_compiler.cpp:693-726 (method call on a property evaluates the base into a temporary; no write-back) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:6283-6297 (4.7 CONFUSABLE_TEMPORARY_MODIFICATION fires only for a statically known native property; untyped $Node bases appear not covered: unverified (needs repro))
frequency: 15 issues with "Line2D points" in the title, at least 7 of them this pitfall (title search); maintainers close them as documented
status: documented; warning added (PR #118002, 4.7) for statically typed bases only
fix_reason: The language can compile mutation of a property rvalue (element store or mutating method) into get, mutate, set using the public property setter, or reject it statically; no engine change needed.

title: Renaming or removing an @export silently discards values saved in every scene and resource
description: Saved .tscn/.tres files store properties by name; after a rename the loader's set() of the old name fails without a message and the next save writes only the new name at its default, so per-instance values across the project are lost; there is no alias or migration mechanism.
example: @export var speed := 5.0  ->  @export var move_speed := 5.0  # every tuned instance reverts to 5.0 when its scene is next saved
evidence_issues: #62643 (closed 2022-07-03, 27 comments; maintainers point to VCS and proposal #3152) | godot-proposals#10644 (open, 42 reactions, 25 comments, "Add an @exported_previously_as() annotation to avoid losing data") | godot-proposals#3152 (open, 23 reactions) | godot-proposals#215 (closed, 17 reactions) | godot-proposals#12423 (closed, consolidated into #10644 and #10694) | godot-proposals#10694 (open, 7 reactions, 23 comments, "Prevent loss of user-entered data in the Godot Editor")
evidence_docs: unverified (no doc statement found; reading gdscript_exports.html found none)
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:567 (node->set(name, value, &valid) during instantiate; valid is never checked, unknown names dropped silently) | core/object/script_language.cpp:615-623 (editor PlaceHolderScriptInstance::set rejects names that have no script default)
frequency: 5 proposals for the same request, top one 42 reactions; #62643 27 comments
fix_reason: A language can declare former names and accept them in its script-instance set callback (re-saved under the new name), and its toolchain can rename across .tscn/.tres; in the editor this needs the language's own inert instance instead of the engine placeholder, still public API (ScriptExtension::_placeholder_instance_create).

title: Values equal to the current default are not stored, so changing a default silently changes saved content
description: Scene packing and the text resource saver omit any property whose value equals the script's (or base scene's) default, so an instance deliberately set to the old default follows a later change of the default; apart from the editor-only Pin Value on instanced scenes there is no way to store such a value explicitly.
example: @export var left_handed := false  # change default to true: every saved character that chose false flips
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#9482 (open, 51 reactions, 21 comments, "Make it possible to explicitly assign the currently default value to an exported property") | #46103 (open, 3 reactions, "Changing default export value type resets every inherited instance")
evidence_docs: unverified (a 2026-03-06 comment on proposal #9482 reports Pin Value is undocumented)
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:1061-1077 (property skipped when equal to default unless pinned) | scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:2099-2103 (.tres saver skips values equal to default) | scene/property_utils.cpp:163-168 (the default comes from Script::get_property_default_value)
frequency: proposal #9482 51 reactions
fix_reason: The default compared against comes from the language (ScriptExtension::_get_property_default_value), so it can stop reporting defaults for fields marked always-stored; a toolchain can list saved files affected by a default change; base-scene defaults stay engine behavior.

title: Typed Array[T] of objects admits null and freed instances; erasing a freed one fails
description: Element validation lets null into any object-typed Array or Dictionary, and only debug builds detect freed instances, by refusing the operation (including erase/find of the stale element) with an error, so Array[Node] cannot be trusted to hold live non-null nodes and cleaning it after free is error-prone.
example: var enemies: Array[Node] = [null]  # accepted / e.free(); enemies.erase(e)  # error, element stays
evidence_issues: #110511 (open, 13 reactions, 10 comments, "Erasing a freed object from a typed array or dictionary fails and prints an error") | #63608 (closed; null into typed Object array) | #72489 (closed; typed arrays with null elements broke deserialization) | related godot-proposals#162 (open, 1038 reactions, nullable static types)
evidence_docs: unverified
evidence_source: core/variant/container_type_validate.h:60-61 (NIL accepted for OBJECT element type) | core/variant/container_type_validate.cpp:54-66 (DEBUG_ENABLED-only freed check: "Attempted to %s an invalid (previously freed?) object instance") | core/variant/array.cpp:356-361 (erase validates its argument first, so a freed element cannot be erased)
frequency: #110511 13 reactions; proposal #162 (general nullability) 1038 reactions
fix_reason: A language can have non-null element types and model freed objects as a checked state in its own typed views; typed Arrays owned by the engine (exports, signals, API returns) keep core validation.

title: Typed arrays are invariant at run time and many APIs return untyped Array: runtime errors and silent no-ops
description: Array.map(), range() and many engine methods return untyped Array, which cannot be assigned or returned as Array[T] even when every element fits (runtime error, no implicit conversion, `as Array[T]` does not convert); a wrong-typed append/insert on a typed array only prints an error and the script continues without the element.
example: var a: Array[int] = [1, 2].map(func(x): return x * 2)  # runtime: Trying to assign an array of type "Array" to a variable of type "Array[int]"
evidence_issues: #72566 (open, 93 reactions, 18 comments; map/filter into typed arrays; #73309, #82538 closed as duplicates) | #72627 (closed, 39 reactions, "Cannot cast typed arrays using type hints") | #86851 (open, 10 reactions, 15 comments; wrong-type append gives no script error and drops the element) | #83026 (open, 10 reactions) | #59721 (open, 9 reactions) | #54311 (open, 8 reactions; as with typed arrays) | godot-proposals#13201 (open, 7 reactions; built-ins should return typed arrays) | godot-proposals#15546 (open, 7 reactions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_array.html#class-array-method-map "returns a new array filled with values returned by the callable" (declared return type Array) | class_array is_typed: "The methods of a typed array are still expected to return a generic Variant."
evidence_source: core/variant/array.cpp:648-650 (map builds an untyped Array) vs :619-622 (filter copies source typing) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:1465 (runtime "Trying to assign an array of type ... to a variable of type Array[...]") | core/variant/array.cpp:280-285 (push_back: failed validate prints via ERR_FAIL_NULL and returns)
frequency: #72566 93 reactions + 2 duplicates; #72627 39 reactions; 131 issues with "typed array" in the title (title search)
fix_reason: A statically typed language can type map/filter generically, insert checked conversions (Array.assign) where engine methods return untyped Array, and make element-type mismatches compile-time or raising errors.

title: Typed collections are one level deep: no Array[Array[int]] or Dictionary[K, Array[V]]
description: Engine container typing stores a single element type (builtin type, class, script), so nested element types cannot be declared, exported or checked; typed Dictionary (4.4) has the same limit plus inspector gaps.
example: var grid: Array[Array[int]]  # not allowed; must be Array[Array]
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#12224 (open, 260 reactions, "Add support for nested typed arrays and dictionaries") | godot-proposals#56 (closed 2024-09-06, 836 reactions; typed Dictionary, shipped in 4.4) | #104581 (open, 21 reactions; exported typed Dictionary key cannot be changed after adding in inspector)
evidence_docs: unverified
evidence_source: core/variant/container_type_validate.h:37-40 (ContainerType = variant_type, class_name, script; no nested element type)
frequency: proposal #12224 260 reactions; #56 836 reactions
fix_reason: A language can type nested generics for its own values and check them statically, but any collection crossing into the engine (exports, signals, API) is a one-level ContainerType unless core changes.

title: In the editor only @tool scripts run; other scripts are inert placeholders and tool mode is not inherited
description: Without @tool a script gets a PlaceHolderScriptInstance in the editor (no code, setters or getters run; only exported values are kept); extending a @tool script without @tool turns tool behavior off; a tool script calling into nodes whose scripts are not tool fails with confusing errors.
example: @tool extends Node / func _ready(): $Child.setup()  # Child's script lacks @tool: placeholder in editor, call fails
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#754 (closed 2024-08-28, 34 reactions, 27 comments, "Warn if script inheriting tool script isn't tool"; GDScript now has a MISSING_TOOL warning) | godot-proposals#3354 (open, 6 reactions, "Provide an informative error message when a tool script is failing due to interacting with a non-tool script") | #36592 (closed, 9 reactions, "Improve error message for calling non-tool scripts from tool scripts") | godot-proposals#520 (open, 6 reactions) | #59745 (C# [Tool] not inherited)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html "The general rule is that any other GDScript that your tool script uses must also be a tool." | same page: "Extending a @tool script does not automatically make the extending script a @tool. Omitting @tool from the extending script will disable tool behavior from the super class." | gdscript_exports.html: "getters and setters will only be used if the script is in Tool mode."
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:1066-1071 (in the editor, can_instantiate() false -> placeholder_instance_create) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:265-267 (can_instantiate needs tool when scripting is disabled in the editor) | modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp:456-457 (MISSING_TOOL warning)
frequency: proposal #754 34 reactions; 250 issues with "tool script" in the title (title search)
fix_reason: Whether a script runs in the editor is decided by the language (ScriptExtension::_can_instantiate, _is_tool, _placeholder_instance_create), so editor execution can be inherited or per member, and calls into non-editor code can be checked statically.

title: @tool runs every callback and setter in the editor, and its edits are saved into the scene without undo
description: With @tool, _ready/_process/_notification and every exported setter execute while editing (setters fire during scene load before children exist), so gameplay code must be fenced with Engine.is_editor_hint(); what the script changes on nodes/resources is saved with the scene, has no undo, and freeing edited nodes can crash the editor or delete work.
example: @tool / func _process(d): position.x += 1  # node drifts in the editor and the drifted position is saved
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#900 (open, 22 reactions, "Provide a keyword to differentiate between tool scripts and plugin code") | godot-proposals#250 (open, 7 reactions, "Protection against accidental, script-triggered node deletion in tool mode (loss of work danger!)") | godot-proposals#9639 (open, 6 reactions; wait for ready before running set on exported properties of tool scripts) | godot-proposals#1539 (closed) | #5983 (open, 37 reactions, "Improve tool script debugging")
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html "Modifications in the editor are permanent, with no undo/redo possible." | "Be extremely cautious when manipulating the scene tree, especially via Node.queue_free, as it can cause crashes if you free a node while the editor runs logic involving it." | "Pieces of code that do not have either of the 2 conditions above will run both in-editor and in-game." | "Changes made by tool scripts and EditorScript (such as adding nodes or modifying properties) do not automatically mark the scene as unsaved."
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:1066-1068 (a tool script gets a real instance in the editor, so all its code runs) | scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:1061-1077 (any non-default value the tool code left is packed on save)
frequency: proposals #900 (22), #250 (7), #9639 (6); #5983 37 reactions; a web search on tool setters running before _ready returned 7+ forum threads in the top 10
fix_reason: The language can define a separate editor-execution model (explicit editor entry points; setters and process callbacks not run in the editor unless declared) and statically flag runtime-only code reachable from it; undo integration stays editor-side.

title: Nodes added with add_child() are not saved (or shown) unless owner is set to the edited scene root
description: PackedScene packing keeps only nodes owned by the root being saved, so nodes created by tool scripts, plugins or runtime code vanish on save; owner must be the edited scene root, not the parent, and nodes under an instanced scene also need editable children.
example: @tool / var m := MeshInstance3D.new(); add_child(m)  # missing: m.owner = get_tree().edited_scene_root
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#390 (open, 32 reactions, 24 comments, "Set owner by default when calling add_child()") | #82756 (closed 2024-01-03, 13 comments; Save Branch as Scene saved children without owner) | #88801 (closed not_planned; reparented nodes lose owner)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node.html#class-node-property-owner "Note: In the editor, nodes not owned by the scene root are usually not displayed in the Scene dock, and will not be saved. To prevent this, remember to set the owner after calling add_child." | running_code_in_the_editor.html: "By default, nodes or scenes added with Node.add_child(node) are not visible in the Scene tree dock and are not persisted to disk."
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:880-882 (_parse_node discards nodes whose owner is not the root being packed, unless an editable instance)
frequency: proposal #390 32 reactions; one web search returned 7+ forum threads on add_child nodes not being saved (e.g. forum.godotengine.org/t/node-that-using-add-child-not-saved/95739, /t/add-child-set-owner-not-permanent-or-visible-in-tree/24411)
fix_reason: A language library can offer a scene-building API that sets owner to the edited root (public Node.set_owner, EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root) and lint bare add_child in editor code; ownership rules themselves are engine.

title: Editing a base scene can silently drop overrides in inherited and instancing scenes
description: Inherited scenes and instances store overrides keyed by node path; before 4.6 renaming or moving a node in the base scene orphaned the derived scene's children and overrides, removing a base node still discards the derived scene's data, and open instances are not refreshed after base-scene edits.
evidence_issues: #16650 (closed 2020, 7 reactions, 14 comments, "Renaming Node Causes Issues in Inherited Scenes") | #82700 and #19520 (closed 2025-10-06 by PR #106837 "Add unique Node IDs to support base and instantiated scene refactorings", milestone 4.6; also fixes #41047, #84928, #97576, #100038, #110518) | #77955 (open, 4 reactions; data loss when removing nodes from the base scene) | #93365 (open, 19 reactions; instances of inherited scenes not updated after a property change) | #90021 (open, 11 reactions) | #24817 (closed by PR #60893 "Rescue orphan nodes in inherited scenes", 4.0; 10 reactions)
evidence_docs: unverified
evidence_source: scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:880-882 and :1153-1154 (what an inherited/instanced scene saves depends on owner and the states stack) | unique-node-ID fallback from PR #106837: location unverified
frequency: 194 issues with "inherited scene" in the title (title search); #93365 19 reactions
status: partly fixed (rename/move: PR #106837, 4.6); removal and refresh issues open
fix_reason: A toolchain can diff a base scene against inheriting/instancing scenes and warn before overrides are orphaned; the storage model and editor refresh are engine/editor code no language controls.

title: Node references in code are strings resolved at run time; renaming or moving a node breaks them silently
description: $A/B, get_node("A/B") and NodePath literals are not tied to the scene file; on rename the editor updates NodePath/Node properties stored in the edited scene but not paths written in scripts, so a rename or reparent appears only as a runtime "Node not found" error and null; Resources cannot hold Node references at all (GDScript now rejects such exports at compile time).
example: @onready var hp_bar = $UI/HPBar  # after moving HPBar under UI/Top: null at run time
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#8465 (closed, 12 reactions; make $ and % use get_node_or_null) | #80538 (closed, 14 comments; exported Node in a custom Resource not resolved) | #76714 (open; error when assigning an exported node to a Resource) | #83011, #82809 (closed; Nodes through Resources) | #83878 (closed; nodes in inherited scene not found via get/set)

title: %UniqueName resolves only within the owner scene, with a surprising fallback to the outer scene
description: %Name is looked up in the calling node's own unique-name map (if it owns nodes), otherwise its owner's; nodes instantiated at run time have no owner, so % from them returns null, while from an instanced sub-scene root a missing name silently resolves to a same-named unique node of the outer scene.
example: @onready var spawner = %Spawner  # in a scene spawned at run time: null
evidence_issues: #107678 (open, 1 reaction, 6 comments, "Unique name search finds node outside the subscene if not found in the subscene") | #92679 (closed 2025-02-03, 18 comments; runtime-instanced nodes get null for % in @onready) | #117871 (closed, 4 comments) | #76614 (closed; branch loses unique name when saved as scene) | godot-proposals#14675 (open, 4 reactions; refactoring when renaming a unique name)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/scene_unique_nodes.html "A scene unique node can only be retrieved by a node inside the same scene." | class_node unique_name_in_owner: "If true, the node can be accessed from any node sharing the same owner or from the owner itself, with special %Name syntax in get_node."

frequency: 40 issues with "unique name" in the title (title search), each <=3 reactions
fix_reason: The owning scene and its unique names are known from the .tscn, so a toolchain can resolve %Name statically and reject uses from runtime-instanced scripts or ones that would hit the outer-scene fallback.

title: Moving or renaming files breaks res:// paths written in scripts; UIDs fix scene references, not string literals
description: When files move, the editor rewrites dependencies stored in .tscn/.tres, but load()/preload() string paths in GDScript are not rewritten, so they fail at parse or load time; UIDs (resources since 4.0, scripts via .uid sidecar files since 4.4) cover uid:// references at the cost of extra files many users want to disable.
example: const Bullet = preload("res://bullet.tscn")  # move bullet.tscn into scenes/ -> script fails to load

status: open (proposal #531); UID mitigation shipped (4.4 for scripts)
fix_reason: A language's own ResourceFormatLoader can implement the public _rename_dependencies virtual to rewrite its path literals when the editor moves files, and its toolchain can check that every literal path exists.

title: Scenes or resources that reference each other (A exports B, B exports A) crash or fail to load
description: An @export PackedScene or preload cycle, such as two levels whose doors point at each other, makes the loader return null or crash, often without a useful message; resources cannot reference each other circularly through exported properties.
example: level1.tscn: @export var next: PackedScene = level2.tscn / level2.tscn: next = level1.tscn
evidence_issues: #24146 (open, 39 reactions, 34 comments, "export var PackedScene crash when having circular references"; reproduced on 4.6.2 in 2026-05) | #80981 (open, 11 reactions), #55409, #74278, #74262, #65057, #35890 (referencing #24146 as duplicate) | godot-proposals#7363 (open, 110 reactions, "Allow circular dependencies/references for resources in export var") | #102073 (open, 7 reactions, cyclic scene preloading) | #98551 (closed duplicate)
evidence_docs: unverified
evidence_source: core/io/resource_loader.cpp:1049-1056 (a load re-entered on the same thread is treated as cyclic and returns null with ERR_BUSY)
frequency: #24146 39 reactions + 6 issues referencing it as duplicate (search "duplicate of #24146"); proposal #7363 110 reactions
fix_reason: A toolchain can detect reference cycles across .tscn/.tres/scripts before run time, and a language can offer lazy scene references (path/uid loaded on first use) instead of eager PackedScene exports; real cycles need loader changes.

title: Hot reload keeps live instances but resets changed members and reruns nothing
description: On script reload (editor save or Synchronize Script Changes in a running game), existing instances keep values only for members with the same name and type; new members and retyped members get an empty value of their type instead of their initializer, _init/_ready/@onready are not rerun, static variables are not updated and lambdas held in members break.
example: var spawn_rate := 2.0  # added during play: live instances get 0.0, not 2.0
evidence_issues: #119057 (open; new Dictionary/Array members stay Nil on live instances, 4.6.2) | #105667 (open, 4 comments; static variables not updated during hot reload) | #97834 (open, 13 reactions, 19 comments; @export_tool_button lambda breaks after edit) | #16974 (closed 2022, 26 reactions, 50 comments; tool script does not call _ready on reload) | #97280 (open, 3 reactions, 23 comments; tool hot reload stops after the first reload) | #24684 (closed; coroutine resumption crash after hot reload)
evidence_docs: unverified
evidence_source: modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2057-2081 (reload_members: keep old value only if same name and type, else construct_empty_value_for_data_type; DEBUG_ENABLED only) | modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2570-2610 (soft reload, saved state re-applied with set()) | core/debugger/remote_debugger.cpp:715 (running game calls ScriptLanguage::reload_scripts)
frequency: #16974 26 reactions, 50 comments; 26 issues with "hot reload" in the title (title search)
fix_reason: Reload is implemented by the language (ScriptLanguageExtension::_reload_scripts/_reload_tool_script, ScriptExtension::_reload), so it can define migration: run initializers for new fields, convert or report retyped ones, and call a declared reload hook.
